location: Section 3.17 line 1554; Section 3.24 line 2409; builder Revision/textbook/notebooks/src/03b_curvature.py lines 161-162 (notebook 03b section 3) and lines 843-844 (caption of Figure 03b.4)
problem: The chapter reads the sign of a plane curvature K(a,b) = R^ab_ab as a shape: positive means curved like a sphere and negative means like a saddle. It applies this to all 28 coordinate planes. In the 4+4 metric, 22 of these planes contain a time-like direction, and there the reading is wrong or reversed. Line 2409 calls the 3-space/extra-time planes 'always saddle-like', and the caption of Figure 03b.4 colours the (x_i, x4) planes red as 'curved like a sphere'.
evidence: Take the plane (x1, x4). Its curvature is K = a4'^2 + a4'' = A^2 H^2 > 0, drawn red ('like a sphere') in Fig. 03b.4. Observers at rest are geodesics (Sec. 3.23). Their deviation along x1 is D^2 xi^1/dtau^2 = -R^1_414 xi^1 = (a4'' + a4'^2) xi^1, and R^1_414 = -a4'' - a4'^2 by the chapter's own case (4). The proper separation e^{AHx4} sin^{1/6}z dx1 therefore grows like e^{A H tau}, so d^2 xi/dtau^2 = +K xi. On the sphere of Sec. 3.18 it is d^2 xi/ds^2 = -K xi: positive curvature focuses there but defocuses here. Further cases: 2-D de Sitter space (K = +1) is a one-sheeted, saddle-shaped hyperboloid. For a plane of two time-like directions (x5, x6), the curvature flips sign relative to the Riemannian metric -g.
fix: Restrict the sphere/saddle picture to planes spanned by two space-like directions, (x_i, x_i') and (x_i, x8). For planes with one time-like direction, state the geodesic-deviation meaning (d^2xi/dtau^2 = +K xi; for example K(x1,x4) = A^2H^2 is the exponential separation of comoving observers). Note that the sign is reversed for a plane of two time-like directions. Delete 'always saddle-like' at line 2409. Fix the words list and the Fig. 03b.4 caption in the 03b builder and rebuild 03b with nbkit build.
